items.title: How ECI's dubious software branded 3.66 crore voters in West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh as suspects
items.shows: From the Commission's own suspect-list summaries, shows software flagged about 1.31 crore West Bengal and 2.35 crore Madhya Pradesh electors for 'logical discrepancies' with no written protocol for resolving them.

items.title: ECI misled the Supreme Court on SIR in West Bengal
items.shows: Uses official records and interviews with election officials to argue that the West Bengal notices were produced in bulk by central software, and that registration officers did not review them one by one as the Commission told the Court.

items.title: How EC Has Quietly Changed Form 6 During SIR, Evading Parliament
items.shows: Traces how the Commission changed Form 6 in each round of the SIR, first adding a declaration in Bihar and later altering the online form itself, with no amendment to the rules. Former Commission officials it quotes say only the government can change the form, under the oversight of Parliament.

items.title: Delhi SIR: With More Than Half the Voters in India's Capital Either Purged or on ECI's Doubtful List, VIPs Get a Pass and the Poorest Pay
items.authors: Shubhangi Derhgawen, Dikshya Koirala, Sumedha Mittal
items.shows: From booth-wise lists of names left off and ground reporting, finds 79.2 lakh of Delhi's 1.45 crore electors were left off the draft or sent a notice, with the heaviest losses among the poorest, including residents of demolished settlements.

items.title: 14 times in 10 months, two Election Commissioners objected on record to poll panel steps
items.shows: From internal notes and letters of November 2025 to August 2026, shows that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi objected on record at least 14 times to SIR decisions, including the Form 6 change, centralised control of the roll software and the West Bengal appeals.

items.title: 'Illegal, unauthorised': Election Commissioners objected to Form 6 change
items.shows: Companion piece showing how a new declaration section was added to Form 6 against the written advice of two Commissioners, who said it needed an amendment to the Registration of Electors Rules.

items.title: No VIP Left Behind: ECI’s Drive to Guarantee a Spot For Them on the Final Voter Roll
items.authors: Ayushi Kar, Shubhangi Derhgawen, Sumedha Mittal, Dikshya Koirala
items.shows: Reports that the Delhi revision gave people the Commission treated as VIPs a separate route onto the roll, through a 'Mark VIP' module in the booth-level officers' app, WhatsApp groups and orders. Ordinary electors with notices were sent to queues and hearings.

items.title: The Mysterious 16.18 Lakh Voters Added to Uttar Pradesh’s Roll
items.shows: Sets the 71.38 lakh Form 6 applications the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer published against the 84.3 lakh electors added to the final roll. It traces the gap to 16.18 lakh applications taken before the draft, whose names and details were never published as the rules require.

items.title: UP CEO Confirms: 16.18 Lakh Applications for Addition Accepted Before Draft Roll. Falsely Claims Details Were Hidden on ECI’s Instructions
items.shows: Follows the earlier report on 16.18 lakh additions in Uttar Pradesh. The state's Chief Electoral Officer confirmed the Form 6 applications were taken before the draft roll and said their details were withheld on the Commission's instructions, and the report sets that against Commission instructions requiring applications after the draft and public details.

items.title: In UP SIR, ECI Software Auto-generated 85,854 Forms to Delete Voters Without a Reason
items.authors: Sumedha Mittal, Ayushi Kar, Shubhangi Derhgawen
items.shows: From the more than 4.3 lakh Form 7 objections the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer published, finds that the roll software generated 85,854 deletion forms giving no reason, carrying the officers' digital signatures. It also counts 1,10,476 deletion requests from individuals accepted after the legal deadline.

items.title: Delhi SIR: ECI Forcing BLOs to Sign Off on Voters Without Verification
items.shows: Reports that booth-level officers in Delhi were told over WhatsApp to clear electors flagged for 'logical discrepancies' by signing a new 'certificate' form. Under this route the flagged cases are closed with no documents and no hearing.

items.title: UP CEO Admits ECI Auto-generated 85,000+ Voter Deletion Forms Without a Reason, Confirms Mass Deletion Attempts Against Muslims
items.authors: Sumedha Mittal, Ayushi Kar (edited by Nitin Sethi)
items.shows: A follow-up to the Collective's investigation of 9 October 2026 into the 85,854 Form 7s that the Commission's software ERONET produced in Uttar Pradesh with no reason for deletion. It reports that the state's Chief Electoral Officer answered on X within minutes, calling the report false, and that evening called it misleading in a recorded video, in which he did not dispute the count or explain why the reasons were missing. It quotes him putting the names targeted by bulk Form 7s at about 4,700 among 13.39 crore electors, and reports that the Commission capped the number of deletion objections one person may file.

items.title: Press Note: Special Intensive Revision - Phase III (No. ECI/PN/086/2026)
items.shows: The Commission's own announcement of the third phase in 16 states and 3 union territories, with its count of booth level officers and agents and its summary of the first two phases.

items.title: 'Differing views' part of 'decision-making', says EC, does not address concerns two ECs red-flagged
items.shows: Reports the Election Commission's first response to the investigation. The Commission calls the 14 notes suggestions and says every decision was unanimous, and the paper sets out what the response does not address.

items.title: Press Note (No. ECI/PN/120/2026): decisions of the meeting of the Commission held on 26.09.2026
items.shows: The Commission's own record of the nine decisions of its full meeting of 26 September 2026. Among them are home visits by booth level officers in place of hearings for electors sent a notice, a review of ECINET by a committee with an outside expert, and later deadlines for claims in Delhi and Maharashtra. It also says the SIR is complete in 20 states and union territories and orders a drive to enrol those left out.

items.title: Press Note (No. ECI/PN/121/2026)
items.shows: Records a Commission meeting attended by all three Commissioners that extended the SIR in Andhra Pradesh (claims and notices to 10 October, final roll on 16 October) and moved Meghalaya's final roll to 26 October 2026.

items.title: Special drive in States/UTs after completion of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) – reg. (Letter No. 23/2025/ERS(Vol-II))
items.shows: The Commission's letter to all Chief Electoral Officers ordering a drive to enrol left-out and young electors. Booth-level officers are to compare the current roll with the pre-SIR roll, list everyone missing, visit each house within about a month, help eligible people fill Form 6 and share the lists with party agents.

items.title: 'SIR Risks Disenfranchising Millions of Legitimate Citizens Over Lack of Documents': Lokniti-CSDS Survey
items.shows: Reports a Lokniti-CSDS survey across Delhi and five states. 52% of respondents had no birth certificate and 41% no domicile certificate, with sharp gaps between states.

items.title: Bihar SIR: Latest ECI data raises more questions over higher deletions among women
items.authors: Areena Arora, Srinivasan Ramani, Vignesh Radhakrishnan
items.shows: Using the list of about 65 lakh Bihar electors left off the draft, which the Supreme Court made the Commission publish, shows women far outnumbered men among those marked 'permanently shifted', most of all below age 40.

items.title: More men die in Bihar, but more women vanish from its voter rolls
items.shows: Sets the Commission's counts of names left off by reason and sex against state death records and finds about 7.6 lakh more women than men left off, including more women entered as dead, although more men die.

items.title: Why exclusion of women voters in Bihar should worry Nitish Kumar
items.shows: Compares Bihar's January 2025 roll with the final SIR roll and finds women were close to 59% of the fall in the roll and the gender ratio of the roll fell in 230 of 243 seats.

items.title: Bihar 2025: In 11 Seats, SIR Deletions Outnumbered Victory Margins
items.shows: Finds 11 Bihar seats where the names left off or deleted exceeded the winning margin, separates the 47 lakh net fall from the 3.66 lakh deleted after the draft, and says the landslide made the numbers moot statewide.

items.title: What Election Commission data says about 'vote chori' in the Bihar elections
items.shows: Checks booth-level results in villages where many names were left off or deleted, the 28 close contests and late additions to the roll, and finds no anomaly that stands out. The NDA won exactly half the close contests.

items.title: After SIR, 13.4% deletions in Gujarat electoral rolls
items.authors: Abhishek Jha, Maulik Pathak, Harsh Yadav
items.shows: Reads Gujarat's final roll of 4.40 crore against the pre-SIR roll, a net fall of 13.4 per cent. The largest falls were in Surat, Ahmedabad and Vadodara and the smallest in the tribal districts of Dang, Chhota Udepur and Narmada.

items.title: Bengal Has 62 Lakh 'Under Adjudication' Electors. Here's Why That Number Is Significant.
items.shows: Sets West Bengal's final roll against the National Commission on Population's projection of adults for 2026 and finds a gap of about 65.7 lakh, with electors at about 91.5% of projected adults.

items.title: More women deleted from rolls in most States after SIR
items.shows: Compares women per 1,000 men on the 2024 Lok Sabha rolls and the final SIR rolls across the second-phase states and finds the ratio fell in every major state except Tamil Nadu.

items.title: Over 61 Lakh Women Dropped from Bengal Voter Rolls, Data Show Stark Gender Bias in SIR
items.authors: Sabir Ahamed, Ashin Chakraborty, Bhanupriya Rao, Souptik Halder
items.shows: From the Commission's lists, finds roughly three in five electors left off, deleted or held under adjudication on West Bengal's roll were women, most heavily in Muslim-majority, Scheduled Tribe and Matua seats.

items.title: 4 tests, 1 question: Did SIR shape Bengal outcome?
items.shows: Runs four tests of the names West Bengal left off or deleted against the 2026 margins and swings. The net count exceeded the BJP's margin in 82 seats but exceeded the swing in margin in only 12 flipped seats, and the names held for adjudication passed the two tests in 49 and 14 seats.

items.title: SIR redraws Bengal’s margins of power
items.authors: Sabir Ahamed, Ashin Chakraborty, Souptik Halder
items.shows: It finds the names left off or deleted in West Bengal's revision outnumbered the winning margin in 161 of 293 Assembly seats, and still did so in 124 seats once deaths are left out.

items.title: SIR exclusions in West Bengal were connected to the AITC lead and Muslim population
items.shows: Using the Sabar Institute's data on names left off or deleted, reports that those names exceeded the margin in 102 of the BJP's 207 seats and, by its own summary, a regression in which they rose with how hard a seat was for the BJP to win.

items.title: Data analysis: How SIR deletions shaped BJP’s landslide in Bengal
items.shows: Sets each West Bengal seat's roll shrinkage against the change in the BJP and TMC margin from 2021 to 2026, and finds each point of shrinkage went with a shift of about 0.38 points toward the BJP. The same test on Bihar finds no such pattern, and the authors describe the Bengal result as an association.

items.title: Comprehensive Analysis of ASDD Deletions in Uttarakhand under the Special Intensive Revision of Electoral Rolls, 2026
items.authors: Sabir Ahamed, Souptik Halder, Ashin Chakraborty
items.shows: It finds at least 8,07,410 names on Uttarakhand's ASDD lists, 52.0% of them women and 57.7% recorded as permanently shifted, more than the 2022 winning margin in 45 of 70 seats.

items.title: Fact Sheet on Voter Deletion Patterns in the West Bengal Special Intensive Revision (SIR), 2025–26
items.shows: Reading 91 lakh elector records, it finds women were 53.6% of the 58 lakh names left off the draft in December 2025 and that in Nandigram, where Muslims are about a quarter of the population, they were 95% of the names deleted from the supplementary lists.

items.title: Preliminary Report on SIR Meghalaya : State-wide analysis of all 60 Assembly Constituencies
items.authors: Sabir Ahamed, Souptik Halder, Ashin Chakraborty
items.shows: It finds 1,80,402 names on Meghalaya's ASDD lists, 8.32% of the draft roll, with death the largest recorded reason at 45.2% and the count above the 2023 winning margin in 32 of 60 seats.

items.title: Bengaluru to Lucknow, why urban centres are seeing high electoral roll deletions during SIR
items.shows: Compares the district with the highest share of names left off in several states: the Bengaluru districts in Karnataka (43 to 49 per cent), Lucknow in Uttar Pradesh, Surat in Gujarat, Chennai in Tamil Nadu, Bhopal in Madhya Pradesh, Gurugram and Hyderabad. A former Chief Election Commissioner and a former Election Commissioner put the pattern down to migration, and the second says that deleting electors for failing to map to the 2002-03 roll would be unfair.

items.title: SIR draft rolls see over 13 crore deletions so far, Delhi leads with 33% left out
items.shows: Tallies the names left off the draft rolls across the states revised so far, over 13 crore, with Delhi the highest at about a third of its roll.

items.title: SIR Draft Rolls Show Highest Voter Deletions in States Where Elections Were Held in Last 3 Years
items.shows: Tabulates the phase 3 draft rolls, 6.15 crore names left off across 17 states and UTs. The five states with the most names left off (Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, Delhi, Andhra Pradesh) all held Assembly elections between 2023 and 2025, and the lowest shares were in Mizoram, Odisha, Manipur, Meghalaya and Sikkim.

items.title: SIR Delhi 2026: The Excluded Roll and the 2025 Verdict
items.authors: Sabir Ahamed, Souptik Halder, Ashin Chakraborty
items.shows: Across all 14,947 polling parts it counts 47,56,722 uncollectable enumeration forms, 32.8% of Delhi's electorate, more than the 2025 winning margin in 68 of 70 seats.

items.title: SIR: Glaring oddities in Maharashtra’s deletion patterns
items.shows: Finds that shifted or absent made up 75% to 96.5% of the names left off in 85 Maharashtra constituencies, and that neighbouring seats in Pune used the two reasons very differently. It estimates that the draft roll falls about 1.92 crore short of the projected adult population.

items.title: SIR: Deletions go up in Phase 3 with more marked as ‘Shifted’ or ‘Absent’
items.shows: Finds that the 17 phase 3 states and territories with draft rolls left off 6.15 crore names, 17.1%, against 12.3% in the first two phases, with a larger share marked shifted or absent. It also finds that the full lists of names left off for Delhi, Maharashtra, Karnataka and Telangana mark no one as 'Others', though the Chief Electoral Officers' press notes put 9.73 lakh names left off in phase 3 under that reason.

items.title: In seat Kejriwal lost by thin margin, nearly 40% names added before 2025 polls missing in SIR draft
items.shows: Follows the New Delhi seat, which had 1,08,788 electors at the 2025 election and lost 37,315 names in the SIR draft. It finds that 560 of the 1,430 voters added in January 2025, about four in ten, are missing from the draft.

items.title: Explainer: Why fewer voters were deleted in Odisha compared to several other states
items.shows: Sets Odisha's net fall of 17.67 lakh (about 5.3 per cent) from the pre-SIR roll to the final roll of 21 September against other states. It gives a 94 per cent return of enumeration forms, few duplicates and mostly seasonal migration as the reasons, and explains how an elector left off or deleted can appeal or reapply.

items.title: SIR Manipur 2026: Preliminary Report on Electoral Roll Deletions
items.authors: Sabir Ahamed, Souptik Halder, Ashin Chakraborty
items.shows: Of the 1,58,677 names left off the draft in Manipur, the 20 hill seats account for 66.4% and women for 55.96%, and women are the majority of those left off in all 60 seats.

items.title: Analysis and Explainer on How the SIR Excluded Voters at Scale
items.shows: Draws on official figures for names left off and an RTI reply on West Bengal appeals. Delhi's draft excluded 32.78% of electors, 91.13% of the decided West Bengal appeals restored the elector, and the public still cannot check the rolls.

items.title: SIR: Telangana may witness net deletion of 70 lakh names or more from electoral rolls
items.shows: Reports that Telangana's draft of 17 August left off more than 73 lakh electors while fresh enrolment applications stayed under 5 lakh, so the net fall may reach 70 lakh. The Chief Electoral Officer's figures show more than 10.2 lakh claims and objections received by 7 October.

items.title: The Link Between TCS, SIR’s Digital Stack, and the Noel Tata-N. Chandrasekaran Tussle
items.shows: Argues that ERONET and ECINET, the roll software Tata Consultancy Services built for the Commission, moved control of the roll away from the registration officers the law names, citing Goa's 97 electors and Uttar Pradesh's Form 7s. It says the links it draws to the Tata group prove no wrongdoing.

items.title: Amid elector apathy, EC extends Maharashtra SIR deadline yet again till October 26
items.shows: Gives the reasons behind Maharashtra's 2.07 crore names left off the draft (7.68 million shifted, 7.55 million absent, 3.48 million dead, 1.76 million duplicates). By 12 October only 8.33 lakh applications and 25,661 Form 7 objections had come in, and 1.22 crore electors on the draft were flagged as unmapped or discrepant.

items.title: Muslims disproportionately flagged in Delhi SIR
items.shows: The Hindu read Delhi's draft roll of 97.54 lakh electors, matched it to the lists of the 33.12 lakh sent notices (13.79 lakh unmapped with the last SIR and 19.33 lakh for logical discrepancies), and guessed each elector's religion from their name and their relative's name. On that guess, Muslims were 13.6% of the draft roll, 7.6% of the unmapped and 20.3% of those flagged for logical discrepancies, and 30% of those flagged for the five reasons that turn on family size, such as six or more electors naming the same parent. The paper reports that ERONET, the Commission's software, decided who was flagged, that no SIR order mentioned notices for discrepancies before the Commission's direction of 14 May 2026, which still did not set out the reasons, and that the Commission had not answered its questions.

items.title: SIR and the BJP's Bengal Majority
items.shows: An economist's counterfactual. Even if every elector deleted after adjudication had voted for the runner-up, the BJP keeps a majority, and only under assumptions the data do not support do the wider counts of names left off or deleted overturn it.

items.title: Power Without Oversight: India’s SIR Judgment and the Unfinished Business of Institutional Design
items.shows: Reads the Supreme Court's SIR judgment against the scholarship on independent electoral bodies and argues that the Commission holds wide power over the rolls without matching accountability.

items.title: How the Invisible Maths of Electoral Roll Revision Altered West Bengal's Election
items.shows: An arithmetic test of sensitivity. The gross count of names left off or deleted exceeded the winning margin in 160 seats, and of two no-SIR scenarios one returns the TMC and the other leaves the BJP with a smaller majority. It does not model voter preference.

items.title: Analysis and Explainer on the Software of the SIR That Runs Without Transparency
items.shows: Describes the systems behind the revision (ECINET, the BLO app, ERONET run by TCS since 2023, the mapping and 'logical discrepancy' rules, machine transliteration and duplicate-detection tools) and finds that none has a published specification, threshold or audit. Citing The Reporters' Collective, it gives 1.31 crore electors flagged in West Bengal and 2.35 crore in Madhya Pradesh by the discrepancy rules.

items.title: Supreme Court Upholds Election Commission's Power To Conduct SIR Of Electoral Rolls, Says It Advances Free & Fair Elections
items.shows: Reports the Supreme Court judgment in ADR v. Election Commission holding the SIR within the Commission's powers and its procedure lawful, with a nexus to free and fair elections.

items.title: Bihar SIR Judgement: Three doctrinal gaps
items.shows: Argues that the judgment of 27 May 2026 relies on one half of the 2024 Section 6A ruling, accepts the Commission's reasons for a special revision without a record behind them, and treats the 1995 Lal Babu Hussein judgment on deletions as limited to proceedings against individual electors.

items.title: Supreme Court wants cases of SIR excluded to be decided before next polls. A reality check from Assam
items.shows: Sets the Supreme Court's direction that exclusions be decided before the next polls against Assam's record. About 3 lakh voters were marked 'Doubtful' in a 1997 revision and 93,000 'D' voters remained before the 2026 Assembly election, with cases held up in Foreigners Tribunals and courts.

items.title: Citizen’s Handbook for Filing SIR Voter Deletion Appeals
items.authors: Sarfaraz Ahmed Khan, Tarique Quasimuddin, Darshana Mitra, Sabir Ahamed
items.shows: It is a step-by-step guide to appealing a deletion from West Bengal's roll before the 19 appellate tribunals set up after the Supreme Court's order, with sample appeals for nine common situations.

items.title: Is ECI Correct In Saying Supreme Court Upheld Its New Form 6 Declaration?
items.shows: Examines whether the May 2026 judgment actually considered the declaration the Commission later added to Form 6, as the Commission claimed.

items.title: Powers of the CEC | Day 1: SC seeks ECI’s response on plea
items.shows: Reports the hearing in which the Court issued notice to the Commission and all three Commissioners on petitions alleging the Chief Election Commissioner took decisions alone, and declined to suspend him in the interim. The Chief Justice said no modified Form 6 had been approved by the Court.

items.title: RTI Reveals: In SIR, Purging of ‘Ineligibles’ from the Voter Lists Might be a Bogey
items.shows: The author asked the Election Commission and the Home Ministry under the RTI Act on 10 August 2026 whether the Commission had referred electors it found not to be citizens to the competent authority under the Citizenship Act, as the Supreme Court ordered in May 2026 to be done within four weeks. The Commission replied after 50 days that it held none of the information. The Home Ministry transferred its application the same day to the Legislative Department, which sent it on to the Commission, and the Commission then passed the questions to the Home Ministry and to the Chief Electoral Officer of Bihar. No reply named the competent authority or gave a number of cases referred.

items.title: ‘Do not put words in our mouth’: Supreme Court says it never adjudicated new Form 6, will examine challenge on Oct 27
items.shows: Reports the bench clarifying that it neither approved nor disapproved the declaration added to Form 6, because it did not exist when the Bihar judgment was given. It sets out the Commission's 26 September claim, the rule-making route under Section 28 of the 1950 Act, and the listing of the challenge for 27 October.

items.title: In India, a Dark Shadow Falls on Its Vaunted Elections
items.shows: A lawyer's essay for an international readership on the protests in Delhi on 10 and 12 October 2026 and how the SIR reached them. It argues that the Supreme Court let the revision become a fact on the ground before ruling on it, then upheld it in 2026 and, in the author's view, freed the Commission from having to act proportionately, and that the Commission's independence was never secured in law. It cites the 90% of decided West Bengal appeals that restored the elector and the Indian Express investigation into the two Commissioners' objections.

items.title: Watch: Bihar SIR: The mystery behind 7 lakh more women elector deletions | Data Point
items.shows: The Hindu's data team sets the gender gap among the names left off Bihar's draft against census migration records and the ages of those left off.

items.title: विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण: वोटर लिस्ट की सफ़ाई के वादे पर वोट देने के मूल अधिकार की कब्र खोदने का इंतज़ाम
items.shows: A Hindi video version of the Collective's Electoral Roll Project findings. Uploaded 5 March 2026, Pacific time (6 March IST).

items.title: Inside The Election Commission: Investigation Finds ECs Split On Key Issues | Indian Express Special
items.shows: The paper's video account of its investigation into the Election Commission. Two Election Commissioners objected on file at least 14 times in 10 months to decisions they said were taken without their knowledge, on deletions, additions, appeals and access to ERONET and ECINET. It also covers the questions added to Form 6, the 97 Goa electors officials could not restore, and the 16 lakh appeals the Commission told the Supreme Court were filed in West Bengal against restored voters.

items.title: Two ECs dissent, questions on legality of SIR process: Constitutional, legal issues & nuances
items.shows: Shekhar Gupta goes through the Indian Express report of the two Election Commissioners' 14 objections, what it shows and what it does not, and the constitutional and legal questions it raises.

items.title: Election Commission Investigation: Ritika Chopra Answers All Your Questions On ECI Investigation
items.shows: The editor who led the paper's investigation into the two Commissioners' objections answers readers' questions: how the software-made 'logical discrepancy' category works, why objections on file by two of three members matter under the law, and what the Commission's reply did and did not deny.

items.title: SIR: 8 Questions, 8 Clear Answers | Election Facts | BJP
items.shows: The BJP's own account of the SIR, answering eight questions on topics the party lists as the 13 crore names, Form 6, ECINET, young voters, the role of the Election Commissioners, 'vote chori' and AI. Its description cites the Commission's published material as saying the SIR is meant to include eligible voters and drop ineligible entries, with claims, objections and appeals, and gives Bihar's final roll as about 7.42 crore.

items.title: “13 Crore Voters Deleted?”| The Real SIR Numbers Explained | #SIR | #BJP
items.shows: A BJP short on the 13 crore names left off the drafts. Its description splits them, citing the Commission's figures, into absent, shifted or other (9.5 crore, 71%), dead (2.7 crore, 20%) and duplicate (1 crore, 7.6%), argues that, given that split, the 13 crore cannot all be read as eligible voters deleted, and points to the Commission's drive to enrol eligible voters who were left out.

items.title: More SIR Deletions, Bigger BJP Swing? Prannoy Roy DeKodes the Data | DeKoder
items.shows: Prannoy Roy sets the names West Bengal left off or deleted beside the 2026 swing against the TMC and argues that they enlarged it. The episode shows no allowance for other differences between seats, and the other analyses of the same question listed here reach different answers.

items.title: Gyanesh Kumar Row: How did the ECI delete 13 crore voters during the SIR | Insight India
items.shows: A conversation with The Hindu's Srinivasan Ramani on how more than 13 crore names came off draft rolls in 30 states and UTs, what the data says about who was left off, and the questions about the exercise's legality.

items.title: Focus on inclusion made Kerala SIR credible | Onmanorama Explains
items.shows: Walks through Kerala's figures: the final roll is 8,97,211 below the 2024 roll (3.24 per cent), more than 98 per cent of the 36.89 lakh unmapped or discrepant electors were kept after hearings, and 92.7 per cent of 14.57 lakh Form 6 applications were accepted. Booth-level officers told the channel they were asked to include as many voters as possible.

dropped.title: Election Commission Row: Is The SIR Process Legally Valid?
dropped.why: studio debate, owner's call to leave out. (oEmbed and watch-next confirm title, NDTV channel, 'Premiered Sep 25, 2026' and the description. The description names no participant and describes 'a heated legal debate' among senior advocates; it is discussion, not reporting.)
